speaker: Ginger
intro: Hello! Ginger Snapp, Crumb and Co. cookies. I brought samples. The snickerdoodles are still warm!
Day 9, trainee: the Case Files. And... are those cookies? Focus, Hoot. Focus.
My customers' voices drop out in the middle. Like a cookie with a bite missing!
A bite missing from the middle? Interesting choice of words. Let's dig in.

options: How long has your hearing been like this?
Since school! The school hearing tests found it. It hasn't really changed since.
Found at school; the same ever since
since_school
Found years ago and stable since. That's a useful clue!
Which cookie is your best seller?
Ginger snaps, obviously. It's practically the law.
Does anyone in your family have hearing trouble?
Dad and Grandma! Their hearing tests look just like mine. A family recipe.
Dad and Grandma have the same pattern
family
Same pattern in the family. Hearing patterns can run in families.
Any ear pain, drainage, dizziness, or sudden change?
None of those. Same as ever, really. I just need to hear my customers now.
No pain, drainage, dizziness or sudden change
no_red_flags
Is it both ears?
Both, about the same. I just smile and nod a lot.
Both ears, about the same
both_ears
Can I have a snickerdoodle?
Of course! *crunch* ...Wait, you're the owl's trainee? Take two.

joke_line: Delicious, but not a clue. Ask about her hearing!

red_flags.ask_line: Always check the red flags: pain, drainage, dizziness, sudden or one-sided change.
red_flags.answer: None of those. Same as ever, really. I just need to hear my customers now.
red_flags.clue: No pain, drainage, dizziness or sudden change
red_flags.card:
Pain, drainage, dizziness, sudden change: NONE.
The same since school.

after_history: Both ears, the same for years, no red flags so far. Let's take a look!

otoscopy.caption: Ginger's RIGHT ear: clear canal, shiny eardrum.
lines: Clear canals, healthy eardrums. Not a single crumb.
A miracle. I'm usually covered in crumbs.

tymp.clue: Tymp: type A both ears (middle ears move fine)
after: Type A both sides: the middle ears move fine. The trouble is deeper in.

instructions: Tell her: press for every beep, even the faint ones.
Like listening for the shop bell. On it!

audiometry.intro: Right ear's yours. Watch the middle pitches!
Left ear at Hoot speed. Same shape?
Bone check at Hoot speed: is it the inner ear?
before: Now the bone buzzer: middle ear or inner ear?

after_audiometry: Bone matches air: no gap. The inner ear, and both sides alike.

reveal.title: COOKIE BITE
lines: Worse in the middle, better at both ends: a cookie bite! It often runs in families.
My ears are SHAPED like my business. That's branding!
Both ears alike, the same since school, and bone matches air.

evidence.prompt: What shape is Ginger's hearing loss?
options: A cookie bite: worst in the middle pitches.
A ski slope: worst in the high pitches.
A noise notch at 4k.
wrong: Look at 4k and 8k: they come back up.
Her dip is wider and lower: 1k to 2k, not 4k.
evidence.right: A cookie bite! The middle pitches carry lots of speech, so voices drop out.

findings.text: Worst in the middle pitches (cookie bite)

lines.fit: Both ears match, stable for years, no red flags: hearing aids tuned for the middle pitches.
lines.refer: No red flags: no pain, dizziness or sudden change, and both ears match. She can be fitted.
lines.today: She's had this since school. Nothing sudden, so no emergency.

clue_pick.prompt: Present the evidence: why is it safe to fit Ginger today?
clue_pick.wrong_line: True, but it doesn't prove she's safe to fit. Look for the red-flag check!
clue_pick.right_line: Exactly! Stable, matching ears, no red flags: fitting is the right call.

payoff: Hearing aids tuned for the middle pitches: right where her bite is.
Oh! I can hear the shop bell AND the customer. Both halves of the cookie!
A family pattern is worth a chat with her doctor some day. Not a red flag, though.
Cookies for everyone! Especially the owl.

headlines.S: COOKIE BITE CRACKED; OWL AWARDED LIFETIME SUPPLY OF SNICKERDOODLES
headlines.A: BAKER HEARS WHOLE CUSTOMERS AGAIN; CRUMB AND CO. CELEBRATES
headlines.Do-over: GINGER BACK TOMORROW WITH MORE SAMPLES

subheads.S: A textbook cookie bite and a perfect call. Free snickerdoodles at the booth.
subheads.A: Stable, matching ears, no red flags: fit and tune for the middle.
subheads.B: The bite showed up; a few stamps crumbled.
subheads.C: Look for the dip between 1k and 2k.
subheads.Do-over: Cookie bites sit in the middle pitches. Ginger brings snacks next time.
